title: Detecting Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity with Calibration Data and a Common Unknown Error Law
banked_reason: The delivered full-class characterization is a bracket: the main-sample exponents are 1/21 versus 4/95, and the calibration exponents are 1/20 versus 2/41, leaving the exact separation function and oracle-retention budget undetermined.
gap_reasons: The stated joint deliverable is a matched explicit minimax separation function and total test, but the current core honestly supplies only unmatched lower and upper envelopes, so the flagship frontier has been replaced by a partial bracket.
The same-class known-channel benchmark required to position the calibration result remains an open bracket rather than an explicit matched oracle rate, leaving the principal comparison incomplete.
Only a necessary retention implication and a sufficient conservative-envelope budget are delivered; the promised necessary-and-sufficient oracle-retention characterization is still open.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved sound conservative joint upper/lower envelopes and necessary-and-sufficient fixed-separation consistency budgets, then pursued a directed maximality round on the shared-calibration moment and actual homogeneous-null mixture. The round established a construction-specific dyadic obstruction and a split-Neumann conditional-mean correction, but the actual-null likelihood denominator blocked a matched main-sample converse. The joint, same-class oracle, and exact oracle-retention frontiers remain open; final math/citation reviews pass, and the independent validity gate concurs with an incremental-tier downgraded bank before formalization.
tldr: The exact oracle, joint and oracle-retention frontiers remain open on the entire stipulated binary causal class. The proved record consists of finite log-free Fourier-profile upper tests, legal calibration and fixed-channel lower witnesses, an if-and-only-if result that fixed-separation consistency requires both budgets to diverge, and the sharp calibration-free public-randomization benchmark. The current joint bracket has lower envelope \(\max\{n^{-1/21},(1+m)^{-1/20}\}\) and upper envelope \(\max\{n^{-4/95},(1+m)^{-2/41}\}\), up to universal constants and finite-budget saturation. A legal exactly homogeneous dyadic-block witness rules out a dimension-free moment envelope for the frozen uncorrected clipped reciprocal profile. A finite split-Neumann correction has a dimension-free centered stochastic term and an explicit deterministic bias bound, with the simpler profile envelope valid when \(m\ge 2^{30}L^4\log(2m)\). Neither construction settles the minimax calibration branch. The note supplies prospective detectable latent mean-heterogeneity benchmarks for binary clinical benefit indicators with separately planned error calibration while retaining the unresolved exact-frontier questions.
gap: Known-channel inverse density tests, two-sample circular density estimation and direct-data rough-nuisance CATE theory do not determine a finite-size detection frontier for the unrestricted constant-CATE null with a shared unknown error law. Recent observed-covariate homogeneity tests do not supply this inverse experiment.
fill: The kernel asks for \(\rho(n,m)\), a certified total test, matching all-randomized-test lower bounds, the same-class known-channel order and necessary-and-sufficient calibration budgets. It combines dependent reciprocal-product control with a convolved homogeneous-null mixture comparison, and treats failure of either proposed route as evidence for corrected rates rather than grounds for a stronger model.
